body: Search is a central component of Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems and has been deeply investigated for classical ASR modeling based on Hidden Markov Models (HMMs). However, in work on current sequence-to-sequence ASR architectures it is often simplified to a small fixed-size beam search without external Language Model (LM). In this work, we present a comparative analysis of search space complexity and efficiency for Connectionist Temporal Classification (CTC) and neural transducer models under different pruning strategies and LM configurations. We show that these end-to-end (E2E) models work with a small search space most of the time but exhibit large temporary peaks in hypothesis count during periods of uncertainty. Score-based pruning dynamically adapts the search to model uncertainty, leading to a significantly lower Real-Time Factor (RTF). Our results highlight the limitations of search with low fixed-size beam pruning and provide practical guidelines for efficient search in E2E ASR.
summaryZh: 时间同步端到端 ASR 模型的搜索空间复杂性和效率的系统比较。搜索是自动语音识别 (ASR) 系统的核心组件，并且已针对基于隐马尔可夫模型 (HMM) 的经典 ASR 建模进行了深入研究。然而，在当前序列到序列 ASR 架构的工作中，它通常被简化为小型固定大小的波束搜索，而无需外部语言模型 (LM)。
